Class 3 · Chapter 3 of 10

Equal parts and fractions

Read shaded fractions, find equal fractions and take a fraction of a group.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Multiply, divide and solve stories. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can read a shaded fraction.
  • I can compare equal fractions.
  • I can find a fraction of a group.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 5

Equal parts

A fraction needs equal parts. Cut the bar into 4 equal parts and shade 1.

We say one quarter, and write 1/4.

Screen 2 of 5

Read a fraction

The bottom number says how many equal parts. The top number says how many are shaded.

Here 3 of 8 equal parts are shaded. That is 3/8.

Screen 3 of 5

Same amount, different names

Half, two quarters and four eighths all cover the same amount.

So 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8. The whole must be the same size each time.

Screen 4 of 5

Compare fractions

With the same whole, more equal parts means smaller parts.

1/3 is bigger than 1/4, because a third is cut into fewer pieces.

Screen 5 of 5

A fraction of a group

Find 1/4 of 12. Share 12 into 4 equal groups.

Each group has 3. So 1/4 of 12 is 3.

Words to know
fraction
A number that shows equal parts of a whole, like 3/8.
numerator
The top number. It says how many parts are shaded.
denominator
The bottom number. It says how many equal parts the whole has.

Chapter passed. Next: Shapes, reflections and boundaries

For parents

What your child learns

A fraction counts equal parts of one whole. The denominator says how many equal parts, and the numerator says how many are counted. With the same denominator, a bigger numerator means a bigger fraction.

A common slip

Children often think a bigger denominator means a bigger fraction, or give the part-to-part count. 1/8 is smaller than 1/4. For a group, the denominator is the whole group.

5-minute home activity: Fold and share

  1. Fold a paper strip into 4 equal parts and shade 1.
  2. Fold another strip into 8 and shade 3.
  3. Line them up and compare the shaded parts.
  4. Put 12 counters in a group and find one third of them.
